results.title: Redesigning Assessments for AI-Enhanced Learning
results.content: Gen AI tools have empowered educators to enhance student engagement, revolutionize assessment methods, develop innovative teaching strategies, and redesign student tasks to align with the demands of the AI era (George & Wooden, 2023; Khlaif et al., 2024). AI-resistant assessments align with educational principles by fostering academic integrity (Kostanek & Li, 2025), inclusivity (Ahmed et al., 2024), and real-world applicability, ensuring that students’ learning outcomes demonstrate human capabilities (Abubakar et al., 2024; Awadallah Alkouk & Khlaif, 2024). The present researchers define AI-resistant assessment as strategically designed evaluation tasks that reduce reliance on Gen AI tools, focus on human-centered critical thinking, creativity, and ethical decision-making skills, and enhance the learning process to prepare students for future jobs. While existing literature highlights challenges like ethical concerns and plagiarism, our research offers a comprehensive framework promoting academic integrity, student engagement, and alignment with 21st-century skills and SDGs. Additionally, it explores AI-resistant assessments to foster critical thinking and adaptability, contextualizing findings within resource-constrained settings to support equitable AI integration in higher education.

results.title: Full article: Artificial intelligence (AI) and ethical concerns
results.content: This research aims to understand the predominant ethical concerns associated with AI systems and technology usage across diverse domains discussed in past studies. *Ethics and Information Technology* has published the most research (forty-four) on AI and ethics, with 1561 citations. Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have become an integral part of our daily lives, and this widespread breakthrough of these technologies in every sphere underscores the urgency and need to examine and address the ethical issues associated with the fair usage of these innovative and intelligent technologies (Munoko et al., Citation2020). Additionally, discussions on regulatory initiatives and the ethical implications of AI systems have increased public awareness, leading to the implementation of proper, stringent measures to safeguard data and deter unauthorized or inappropriate use, including anonymization and data encryption (Larson et al., Citation2020). Through its thorough bibliometric and thematic analysis, this research helps understand the ethical dilemmas concerning AI systems through diverse theoretical dimensions, providing a more holistic view of the field.
